Low-level likelihood and derivatives at one parameter value

Source: R/radish_algorithm.R
terradish_algorithm.Rd

Calculates likelihood, gradient, Hessian, and partial derivatives of a parameterized conductance surface, given a function mapping spatial data to conductance and a function mapping resistance distance (covariance) to the genetic response. This is the evaluation that terradish calls at every optimizer step; most users never call it directly. The approach of fitting one parameterized surface is described by Peterman and Pope (2021).

Usage

terradish_algorithm(
  f,
  g,
  s,
  S,
  theta,
  nu = NULL,
  phi = NULL,
  objective = TRUE,
  gradient = TRUE,
  hessian = TRUE,
  partial = TRUE,
  nonnegative = TRUE,
  validate = FALSE,
  cores = 1L,
  curvature = c("exact", "gauss_newton"),
  solver = c("direct", "auto", "amg"),
  solver_control = NULL,
  solver_warm_start = NULL,
  solver_reuse_state = NULL,
  measurement_control = NULL,
  worker_pool = NULL
)

Arguments

f

A function of class "terradish_conductance_model", as returned by a conductance-model factory such as loglinear_conductance (see terradish_conductance_model_factory).

g

A function of class "terradish_measurement_model" (see terradish_measurement_model).

s

An object of class "terradish_graph"

S

A matrix of observed genetic distances or covariance, as required by g

theta

Parameters for conductance surface (e.g. inputs to 'f')

nu

Effective Wishart degrees of freedom, passed through to measurement models that require it.

phi

Optional warm-start values for the nuisance-parameter subproblem.

objective

Compute negative loglikelihood?

gradient

Compute gradient of negative loglikelihood wrt theta?

hessian

Compute Hessian matrix of negative loglikelihood wrt theta?

partial

Compute partial derivatives of negative loglikelihood wrt theta and spatial covariates/observed genetic distances

nonnegative

Force regression-like 'measurement_model' to have nonnegative slope?

validate

Numerical validation via 'numDeriv' (very slow, use for debugging small examples)

cores

Number of worker processes to use for per-parameter derivative calculations. 1 evaluates serially.

curvature

Which curvature to return in hessian. "exact" (default) returns the exact Hessian of the negative log-likelihood. "gauss_newton" returns the Gauss-Newton / Fisher-information approximation, obtained by dropping the two residual-weighted second-derivative terms (the second derivative of the resistance covariance \(E\) and of conductance with respect to theta). It is an information-based approximation and is positive semidefinite when the retained measurement-model curvature is positive semidefinite. It equals the exact Hessian only when the omitted terms are zero or negligible; convergence alone does not guarantee equality. A large gap can reflect residual structure, model mismatch, or numerical instability and should be investigated rather than assigned a unique cause. It also requires only first derivatives of the conductance model, which is useful for Gaussian scale-aware and spline conductance models whose second derivatives are expensive or unstable. The number of linear solves is the same as for the exact Hessian.

solver

Linear-system solver. "direct" uses sparse Cholesky, "amg" uses algebraic multigrid, and "auto" chooses between them.

solver_control

Optional named list of solver settings. For solver = "direct", supported entries include factorization ("auto", "simplicial_ldl", "simplicial_ll", or "supernodal_ll"), solve_backend ("matrix" or the experimental "cholmod_cpp" and "cholmod_cpp_cached" backends), supernodal_min_vertices, supernodal_max_rhs, and perm. For solver = "auto", supported selection entries include auto_direct_max_vertices, auto_amg_min_vertices. The legacy auto_direct_max_rhs is ignored. For solver = "amg", supported entries include tol, maxit, coarse_enough, npre, npost, sa_relax, aggr_eps_strong, estimate_spectral_radius, power_iters, and reuse_preconditioner. reuse_preconditioner_max_age can be set to a finite nonnegative value to periodically rebuild the AMG hierarchy instead of reusing it indefinitely. Direct solvers also accept reference = "auto" (default), which grounds a maximum-conductance vertex when the conductance ratio exceeds one million, or "last" and "max_conductance". This changes the numerical reference potential while preserving the graph and model. It improves some stiff solves but cannot guarantee accuracy at arbitrary conductance contrasts. Direct solves check the maximum absolute residual in each right-hand side, divided by its maximum absolute input or one, whichever is larger. residual_tolerance = 1e-8 rejects unresolved systems by default; Inf disables this check for diagnosis. A small residual is necessary but does not guarantee small forward error on an ill-conditioned graph. Before rejection, refinement_steps = 3 permits up to three correction solves using the same factorization and the current residual. Direct supernodal factorizations can benefit from a threaded BLAS, but the relevant thread counts are controlled by the external R/BLAS build rather than by terradish_algorithm(). If the direct solver stops with a CHOLMOD or non-positive-definite reduced Laplacian message, the current conductance values made the graph numerically singular. Check for missing or infinite raster covariates, use scaled covariates and moderate starting values near zero, and try solver = "auto" or solver = "amg" while diagnosing the fit.

solver_warm_start

Optional initial guess for the reduced-system solve. This is primarily useful for iterative solvers when evaluating nearby parameter values.

solver_reuse_state

Optional reusable solver state returned by a prior terradish_algorithm() call. This is used to reuse AMG hierarchy information or compatible direct CHOLMOD factorization state across nearby evaluations.

measurement_control

Optional NewtonRaphsonControl object used to profile nuisance parameters. The default retains the package's high-accuracy profiling tolerances.

worker_pool

Optional reusable worker pool created internally by terradish. Most users should leave this as NULL.

Value

A list containing at a minimum:

covariance

rows/columns of the generalized inverse of the graph Laplacian for a subset of target vertices

Additionally, if 'objective == TRUE':

objective

(if 'objective') the negative loglikelihood

phi

(if 'objective') fitted values of the nuisance parameters of 'g'

subproblem

(if 'objective') convergence code and iteration count for the nuisance-parameter profile

boundary

(if 'objective') is the solution on the boundary (e.g. no genetic structure)?

fitted

(if 'objective') matrix of expected genetic distances among target vertices

gradient

(if 'gradient') gradient of negative loglikelihood with respect to theta

hessian

(if 'hessian') Hessian matrix of the negative loglikelihood with respect to theta

partial_X

(if 'partial') Jacobian of the gradient with respect to the spatial covariates

partial_S

(if 'partial') Jacobian of the gradient with respect to the observed genetic distances

References

Peterman WE, Pope NS (2021). The use and misuse of regression models in landscape genetic analyses. Molecular Ecology, 30, 37–47. doi:10.1111/mec.15716 .

See also

terradish, terradish_grid

Other model fitting: conductance(), terradish(), terradish_distance(), terradish_grid(), terradish_methods

Examples

# \donttest{
library(terra)

data(melip)
covariates <- c(terra::unwrap(melip.altitude),
                terra::unwrap(melip.forestcover))
coords <- terra::unwrap(melip.coords)
names(covariates) <- c("altitude", "forestcover")
# Coarsened so the example runs quickly; name layers, then scale.
covariates <- scale_covariates(terra::aggregate(covariates, fact = 3,
                                                na.rm = TRUE))
# Keep one site per raster cell (some melip sites share a cell).
keep <- !duplicated(terra::cellFromXY(covariates, terra::crds(coords)))
Fst <- melip.Fst[keep, keep]
surface <- conductance_surface(covariates, coords[keep])
conductance_model <- loglinear_conductance(~ altitude + forestcover, surface$x)

# One evaluation at theta = (-0.3, 0.3): negative log-likelihood, its
# gradient and Hessian with respect to theta, and the profiled nuisance
# parameters.
value <- terradish_algorithm(conductance_model, leastsquares,
                             surface, Fst, theta = c(-0.3, 0.3))
value$objective
#> [1] -1375.273
value$gradient
#> [1] -94.60471  51.19362
value$phi
#>              [,1]
#> alpha -0.01942733
#> beta   0.31180555
#> tau    6.91515095
# }
